correctness.rationale: Canonical digit pairing reduces odd palindromes to a signed linear form. The finite Fourier transform has three exhaustively separated kinds of frequencies: zero gives \((b-1)b^k\), half the modulus when even gives \((b-1)b^{k-1}\), and all other frequencies give \((-1)^{k+1}(\zeta^h+\zeta^{-h})\). Direct orthogonality gives the exact formula; the residue-by-residue correction is strictly inside \((-1,1)\) including \(q=2\). One-digit and even lengths are independent direct counts. The original standalone verifier passed 1204 exact independent residue comparisons for bases 2–14, all dividing moduli, and lengths 1–7. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The new exact count, all-residue Fourier spectrum, and strict unit discrepancy for odd digit lengths and moduli dividing the base plus one were compared to three pertinent primary full texts. The 2004 estimates and 2009 main theorems assume coprimality to the base and its square-minus-one; the 2009 sieve Lemma 22 does include some exceptional prime divisors of the base plus one in averaged zero-residue estimates, but not this exact fixed-length theorem. The 2024 exact-count work handles bases congruent to zero or one modulo the modulus. The modulus-two intersection, the known even-digit obstruction, and odd-prime qualitative equidistribution are not claimed novel. An unstated consequence or unindexed equivalent may remain.

value.rationale: Distribution of canonical palindromes over congruence classes is an established explicit counting problem. Earlier natural branches \(b\equiv0,1\pmod q\) have exact formulas while the exceptional \(b\equiv-1\pmod q\) branch was outside those results. The new statement classifies all residues and all digit lengths in that branch, has strict absolute discrepancy below one, and exposes persistent bias for even moduli via an exceptional Fourier character. Neither basic even-digit divisibility nor qualitative odd-prime uniformity is used as the claimed new value.
